to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on

————
(Ministries : Prime Minister; Agro and Rural Industries; Atomic Energy; Coal;
Communications and Information Technology; External Affairs; Labour and
Employment; Ocean Development; Overseas Indian Affairs; Personnel, Public

Road link to Myanmar
*261. SHRI MATILAL SARKAR: Will
the Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are
contemplating to take initiative in extending
road-links to Myanmar across the North-
Eastern States according to the 'look east'
policy;
(b) if so, the response received from
other countries; and
(c) if not, whether any other similar
programme is being contemplated?
 Directors in Neyveli Lignite
Corporation
*262. SHRIMATI AMBIKA SONI:
SHRI SANTOSH
BAGRODIA:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Board of
directors of Public Sector Undertakings are
to consist of 50 per cent directors and non-
executive directors but in the Neyveli
Lignite Corporation (NLC) there was only
one independent director on its board as
has been reported by C&AG in its report
No. 4 of 2003 (PSUs);
(b) if so, the reasons for violating SEBI's
rule and the steps taken to rectify the
mistakes and to fix the responsibility of
the authority concerned for their being no
non-executive director; and
(c) the details of other observations
made by C&AG regarding NLC and the
action taken thereon?
 Contribution for earthquake
rehabilitation from
MPLADS fund
*263. SHRI LALITBHAI MEHTA:
Will the Minister of STATISTICS AND
PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION
be pleased to state:
(a) the amount collected by way of
contributions made by Rajya Sabha MPs

82
for earthquake rehabilitation works in
Gujarat from their MPLADS funds;
(b) the details of works carried out by
HUDCO and NBCC and the amount spent
as on the 30th June, 2005 by these agencies;
(c) whether ten Community Halls in
Wankaner Taluka villages were sanctioned
and work orders given by NBCC;
(d) if so, the progress made in the
construction of those Community Halls;
and
(e) the amount lying with HUDCO,
NBCC and the Ministry, with interest as
on the 30th June, 2005, out of the collection
made?
 Impact of tsunami
*264. SHRI JANARDHANA
POOJARY: Will the Minister of SCIENCE
AND TECHNOLOGY be pleased to
state:
(a) whether any scientific analysis has
been carried out for ascertaining the impact
and havoc brought by the recent tsunami in
the country;
(b) if so, the details in this regard;
(c) the measures that are contemplated
to forecast tsunami and such other disasters
in future and to meet the challenges thrown
by such disasters in the future;
(d) whether experts have suggested
creating mangroves on the shores to
minimize the impact of tsunami; and
(e) if so, the details in this regard and
Government's reaction thereto?
 Tokyo-led Asian Broad Band
Programme
*265. SHRI KARNENDU
BHATTACHARJEE: Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that India and
Japan have signed an MoU for participation
of India in the Tokyo-led Asian Broad Band
Programme; and
(b) if so, the details of the agreement?
 Water harvesting
*266. SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of STATISTICS AND
PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that it is proposed
to make water harvesting a part of
MPLADS to control water crisis in the
country;
(b) if so, the details of the action plan;
and
(c) how far this would help to address
this issue?
 Upgradation of Telephone Exchanges
in Mizoram
*267. SHRI LALHMING LIANA: Will
the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) the number of Telephone Exchanges
with their capacity in the State of Mizoram
and the exchanges which are earmarked for

83
upgradation during the current financial
year;
(b) whether BSNL is contemplating to
cover the whole State of Mizoram with
WLL during the financial year 2005-06; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
 National Ship Design and Research
Institute
*268. SHRI S.M. LALJAN BASHA:
Will the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) the present role of the NSDRI in
Vishakhapatnam;
(b) the funding provided by
Government to the NSDRI over the last
three years, year-wise;
(c) whether it is a fact that the work
load and work output of NSDRI is totally
inadequate;
(d) whether Government propose to
wind up the Institute;
(e) if so, whether Government would
hand over the NSDRI to Andhra
University; and
(f) if not, the reasons for funding of
NSDRI?
 War against terrorism by Pakistan
*269. SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: Will
the Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that JKLF leader
Yasin Malik confessed before the media
during his visit to Islamabad in June, 05
that Pakistan Information Minister is the
person in-charge of terrorist training camps
across our international border;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether the ground reality, revealed
by the confession, has been contrary to the
assurances given by the Pakistan President
in January, 2004;
(d) whether Government confronted
Pakistani administration with it, besides
the international community engaged in war
against terrorism; and
(e) if so, the details thereof, including
response of the respective Governments
in this regard?
 Recruitment of drivers by KGL
*270. SHRI ANAND SHARMA: Will
the Minister of OVERSEAS INDIAN
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government's attention has
been drawn to the renewed activities of
Kuwait and Gulf Link Transport Company
of Kuwait to recruit drivers and other
categories of workers for Iraq; and
(b) if so, the steps taken by Government
to safeguard Indian citizens from being lured
into hazardous employment in Iraq?
 Country among maritime nations
*271. PROF. SAIF-UD-DIN SOZ: Will
the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether despite the long coastline,
India is not rated among the top 20 maritime
nations; and
(b) if so, the measures that Government
would adopt to improve the situation?

84
 Power target through existing
reactors
*272. SHRI B.J. PANDA:
SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that by 2020,
India plans to be a nuclear reactor global
leader;
(b) if so, the details of the action plan to
achieve the target;
(c) the quantity of power produced by
the existing reactors; and
(d) the power target by 2020 through
these reactors?
 Short-term coal linkage to power
sector
*273. PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that short-term
coal linkages to nearly 90 power sector
units for the second quarter of 2005-06 has
been approved;
(b) if so, whether allocation is 4.26
million tonne more than what was
approved for the corresponding period of
2004-05;
(c) whether a special group of his
Ministry has been asked to continuously
monitor performance of various power
utilities and make additional allocations
whatever required for power; and
(d) if so, to what extent these power
projects have received coal to meet the
shortages?
 ESI hospitals
*274. SHRI S. ANBALAGAN: Will the
Minister of LABOUR AND
EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the number of super speciality
hospitals administered/directly run by
ESIC, State-wise;
(b) whether Government propose to
open more such super speciality hospitals
in near future;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) the number of State Government
run hospitals of ESIC, State-wise;
(e) whether it is a fact that services
provided by ESIC are not properly
implemented due to dual Control of
both the State and Central Governments;
and
(f) if so, the details thereof and the steps
proposed to be taken thereon?
 Minimum wages for Agricultural
Labourers
*275. SHRI N.R. GOVINDARAJAR:
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND
EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have
conducted any survey for determination of
the existing number of Agricultural workers
in the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof male, female
separately, State-wise;
(c) the rate of minimum wages
prescribed for them and the manner in which
it is implemented;
(d) whether Government are considering
the revision of existing minimum wages for
agricultural labourers; and

85
(e) if so, the details thereof?
 Construction of National Highway in
Bihar
*276. SHRI MOTIUR RAHMAN: Will
the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
construct a National Highway from Chakia
to Bairgania and Motihari to Sitamarhi in
Bihar;
(b) whether construction of such a road
is necessary in the interest of security of
the country; and
(c) if so, the steps being taken to
expedite the work?
 Generating employment in
Maharashtra
*277. SHRI SANJAY RAUT: Will the
PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the problem
of unemployment is increasing day by day
as well as employment in the organised
sector is also declining in the last two years
in the country particularly in the
Maharashtra State;
(b) if so, Government's response and
reaction thereto;
(c) whether Government are considering
any specific programmes for generating
more employment in the country specially
in the Maharashtra State during the next
three years; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
 Opening of Still Well road
*278. SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA:
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that China and
India have lately been actively working on
plans to reopen the still well road between
the two countries through Myanmar, which
would reduce the distance between the two
nations from over 6,000 kms. to just 1300
kms.;
(b) if so, the decision taken in the matter
and the respective stand of India, Myanmar
and China in regard thereto and how the
benefits of increase in trade and facilities
would be stored; and
(c) the steps taken and are being taken
in this regard so far?
 Boats seized by Pakistani Security
Agency
*279. SHRI LEKHRAJ BACHANI:
PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA:
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the continuous problem of Indian fishermen
and boats being taken into custody by the
Pakistani Security Agency;
(b) if so, the steps proposed to be taken
to resolve this matter; and
(c) whether Government propose to
sign an agreement with the Pakistani
Authorities on the lines of the agreement
between India and Sri Lanka?

86
 Sports facilities in Lucknow
†*280. SHRI BHAGWATI SINGH:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the State Government of
Uttar Pradesh had sent projects for the
construction of judo hall, volley ball indoor
hall and shooting range in Guru Gobind
Singh Sports College, Lucknow, for the
approval of Government;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) whether Government have given
approval to the aforesaid projects, if not,
by when these are likely to be approved?

National Programme on Rural
Industrialisation
1884. SHRI DWIJENDRA NATH
SHARMAH: Will the Minister of AGRO
AND RURAL INDUSTRIES be pleased
to state:
(a) the present status of National
Programme on Rural Industrialisation in the
State of Assam;
(b) the details of the allocation of funds
made by Government during the last three
years and whether it has been fully spent
by the State; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Ban on technology and materials
1885. SHRI B. K. HARIPRASAD: Will
the Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether India’s inability to expand
its present nuclear power generation
capacity, which cover only 3 per cent of
our total requirements is due to inadequate
supplies of uranium and technological
assistance coupled with embargo by a cartel
called Nuclear Suppliers Group (NSG);
(b) whether the NSG operates a blanket
ban on technology and materials trade with
black-listed countries, including India; and

the ban currently in force?
Accident in CCL mine in Hazaribagh
1886. SHRI LALIT SURI:
SHRI DARA SINGH
CHAUHAN:
Will the  PRIME  MINISTER be
pleased to state:
(a) whether a number of workers got
trapped inside the Central Coal Fields Ltd.
(CCL) Saunda mine in Hazaribagh on the
14th June, 2005;
(b) the number, out  of them, who lost
their lives and those who could be rescued;
(c) whether the cause of the accident

through outsourcing by Coal India Limited
and its subsidiaries during the last three
years?

MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that his Ministry
and Coal India Limited are considering an
IPO to part finance its Rs. 21,000/- crores
investment plans; and
(b) if so, the details thereof?

Coal fields Limited has launched e-auction

against the open sale scheme;

coal supply in the country, more so in
Orissa;
(b) if so, whether as a result of this
industrial production of iron, steel and other
metals have been affected severely; and
(c) what are the reasons for this shortage
despite a vast reserve of coal of 250 billion
tonnes and lignite of 36 billion tonnes in
the country?

entrusted to ESM (Ex-servicemen)
companies;
(b) if so, the names of these companies;
(c) the amount paid to these companies

three years; and
(d) the rate of loading with a Surface
Miner Machine and the rate paid to the
ESM companies?

the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to

have taken a decision to invest in

methane (CBM) and underground coal
gasification (UCG);
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that
Government have envisaged CBM
production and UCG equivalent to 25
million tonnes of coal by 2025; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?

the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to

coal mines has increased due to overlooking

Government to prevent these accidents?

SHRI LEKHRAJ BACHANI:
Will the Minister of

INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be

(a) whether the aim of Department of
Posts is to provide services or to earn profit;
(b) the number of post offices which
have been closed in Gujarat during the last
five years and the reasons therefor; and

any plan to appoint any agent at those
places where post offices have been closed?
Provision of Rural Telephones in
Gujarat
†1898. SHRI JAYANTILAL BAROT:
SHRI LEKHRAJ BACHANI:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the fact that Rural Telephones are not being
made available by private phone companies
(Basic Operators) in certain districts of
Gujarat;
(b) if so, the steps taken in this regard;
(c) if not, the reasons therefor; and
(d) the names of the villages where such
a facility is not available?
Funds allocated for telecom circle in
Maharashtra
1899. SHRI KRIPAL PARMAR:
SHRI BALAVANT ALIAS
BAL APTE:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) the details of the funds allocated for
providing telecom services in Maharashtra
for each of the last three years and the
current financial year, district-wise;
(b) whether the telecom circles have
achieved their targets;
(c) if so, the details thereof including
the expenditure incurred thereon;
(d) if not, the reasons therefor; and
(e) by when the target is likely to be
achieved?
Poor performance of BSNL
1900. SHRIMATI KAMLA
MANHAR:
SHRI DHARAM PAL
SABHARWAL:
SHRI RAJU PARMAR:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Bharat
Sanchar Nigam Ltd. (BSNL) and
Mahanagar Telephone Nigam Ltd. (MTNL)
are way behind private sector providers in
terms of Quality of Service (QoS)
parameters;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons therefor;
(c) whether inspite of poor performance
by BSNL, Government are extending full
financial support by way of Access Deficit
Charges to the tune of several crores of
rupees; and
(d) if so, the reasons therefor?
Restructuring of postal network
1901. SHRIMATI JAMANA DEVI
BARUPAL: Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND INFOR-
MATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government have roped in
global consultants KPMG to prepare a
report on restructuring the postal network
across the country;
(b) whether the mandate given to
KPMG includes identifying new areas of
business;
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

431
(c) whether the i dea behind this
restructuring is to wipe out Rs. 1400 crores
deficit;
(d) whether following this review the
prices of postal products barring some
essential common man items such as inland
letters, envelopes and post cards could be
increased to market rates; and
(e) if so, to what extent this revamping
of postal network would be helpful?
Incentives to Telecom Services
Providers
1902. DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
Will the Minister of COMMUNI-
CATIONS AND INFORMATION
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether Telecom Regulatory
Authority of India has pointed out that
Government needs to increase the level of
competition in the rural sector by offering
incentives to Telecom Services
Providers;
(b) if so, whether the TRAI has
highlighted that the operators would be
required to add 4 million new users every
month compared with just around 1.5
million at present to achieve the target set
by Government;
(c) if so, whether this is possible only if
telephone services were made available in
the rural segments;
(d) if so, what are the other points made
in the study paper of TRAI; and
(e) to what extent Government have
accepted the proposal and the steps taken
to boost the rural telephones in the
country?
Amendment in the Indian Telegraph
Act
1903. SHRIMATI  AMBIKA SONI:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI
REDDY:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
amend the Indian Telegraph Act to facilitate
mobile operators roll out networks in rural
areas for sharing infrastructure i.e. funded
by the Universal Service Obligation (USO)
Fund;
(b) whether Government have already
discussed the matter with USO Fund
administration and has worked out the
details;
(c) whether amendment to Telegraph
Act is necessary to accommodate  the
basic cellular and other wireless
technologies;
(d) whether the main purpose is to
construct towers in rural areas, so that,
cellular and CDMA lines can reach villages;
and
(e) if so, by when Government are likely
to amend the Indian Telegraph Act?
Provision of satellite phones to
subscribers

KHANDELWAL: Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND INFOR-
MATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government propose to

432

provide satellite phones to all the applicants
of rural areas listed in waiting list by March,
2006; and
(b) if not, Government’s intention in
this regard?
Role of post offices in banking
operations
1905. SHRI R.P. GOENKA: Will the
Minister of COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is a
proposal to redefine the role and activities
of the post offices to, inter-alia, undertake
some of the banking operations across the
country;
(b) if so, the details thereof, and its
present status; and
(c) the details of schemes drawn up to
create the required infrastructure in post
offices and to suitably upgrade the skills of
the selected postal staff who would handle
their new responsibilities as also machinery
proposed to be established to provide the
required level of expertise in managing and
deploying large funds likely to be mobilized
by the postal banks?
Smart city project
1906. SHRI A. VIJAYARAGHAVAN:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the smart city project,
conceptualized in Ernakulam district of
Kerala is under the Information Technology
Policy of State;
(b) if so, whether Dubai Internet City
(DIC), the company behind the above
project is an IT company or an IT park;
(c) whether DIC is owned by UAE
Government;
(d) if so, whether DIC is eligible to get
concession under the State Information
Policy; and
(e) the details in Memorandum of
Understanding signed with DIC for the
smart city project?
Unwanted phone calls
†1907. SHRIMATI SUSHMA
SWARAJ: Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the fact that mobile phone subscribers are
facing a lot of problems  due to the
unwanted phone calls;
(b) whether the Supreme Court has also
issued any guidelines to provide relief to
the subscribers in this regard; and
(c) if so, the action being taken by
Government to ensure the observance of
the said guidelines?
Safeguarding customer’s phone
numbers
1908. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI: Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether any concrete steps have
